import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import io

# Prepare the dataset
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a professional and clean style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a multi-dimensional scatter plot (bubble chart)
# This allows us to encode several variables into one graphic:
# - X-axis: Price (a key decision factor)
# - Y-axis: Megapixels (a key performance metric)
# - Color: Brand (for easy comparison)
# - Size: Max ISO (another key performance metric for low light)
# - Marker Style: Body Type (to differentiate camera categories)
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    hue='brand',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2500),  # Emphasize the difference in ISO capabilities
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Annotations and Customizations for Clarity ---

# Add text labels for each point to provide specific context, as the dataset is small
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'] + 70,  # Offset text for readability
        row['megapixels'],
        f"{row['brand']} ({row['model_year']})\n{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontsize=11,
        fontstyle='italic',
        color='black',
        va='center'
    )

# Set an insightful title and clear axis labels
ax.set_title('Camera Analysis: Price vs. Megapixels and ISO', fontsize=22, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)

# Format the x-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Improve and reposition the legend to avoid overlapping data points
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Split the legend into two parts for better organization
brand_body_count = len(df['brand'].unique()) + len(df['body_type'].unique())
legend1 = ax.legend(h[:brand_body_count+1], l[:brand_body_count+1], bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1), loc='upper left', title='Brand & Body Type')
ax.add_artist(legend1)
legend2 = ax.legend(h[brand_body_count+1:], l[brand_body_count+1:], bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 0.55), loc='upper left', title='Max ISO')

# Adjust plot limits to ensure all elements are visible
ax.set_xlim(left=0, right=df['price_usd'].max() * 1.15)
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0, top=df['megapixels'].max() * 1.15)
ax.grid(linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Use tight_layout and adjust subplot parameters to make space for the external legend
plt.tight_layout()
plt.subplots_adjust(right=0.78)

# Save the resulting high-quality figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

plt.close()
